alternatives.condition: If the missing operative wording makes both confirmation and demonstration conditional on an SFC request.
alternatives.consequence: Absent a request, those request-dependent duties would not be triggered by that wording alone. That would not establish compliance with independent substantive or continuing duties.

alternatives.condition: If the request qualifier attaches only to demonstration, while confirmation is required independently.
alternatives.consequence: Absent a request, the demonstration duty would remain untriggered, but the independent confirmation duty would remain applicable. The delivered evidence does not establish that this is the correct reading.

alternatives.condition: If the missing wording distinguishes an ongoing substantive standard from an obligation to provide confirmation or evidence on request.
alternatives.consequence: Absence of a request would affect the request-dependent submission obligation, not necessarily the underlying standard. The operative text is needed to establish whether this distinction applies.

assumptions: The absence of an SFC request is treated as the question's conditional premise, not as an independently verified client fact.
The conditional alternatives identify interpretive possibilities to test against the missing text; they are not source-supported rival constructions established by the delivered extracts.
conclusion: The delivered evidence does not establish how the request trigger attaches to confirmation and demonstration, what each act concerns, or what standard each must satisfy. It also does not permit a comparison of the succeeding operative provisions. Those texts and the relevant footnote are missing. Accordingly, the absence of an SFC request establishes neither a general exemption nor compliance or breach on this record. The supplied substantive extract reserves the possibility of further guidance or additional requirements; it does not establish that any particular additional requirement has been imposed. The clarification route, institutional names, download link and page-update metadata do not supply the missing legal test.

unresolved: The complete request-dependent clause and its footnote are needed to determine whether the request qualifier governs both acts, only one act, or a separate evidential obligation. Their syntax, cross-references and context have not been supplied.

The object of confirmation, the object of demonstration, the required degree of assurance or proof, the responsible actor and the recipient remain unverified. Neither act can be equated with satisfaction of the underlying legal standard without the operative wording.

The complete text of both succeeding operative provisions is needed to compare their actors, triggers, substantive duties, evidential requirements and timing. The later of those provisions has no offered source-gap selector; its absence is recorded here without inventing one.

The effect of no request on any independent or continuing duty remains unresolved. A request-dependent obligation must be distinguished from retained responsibility, required supervisory conduct and required operational outcomes.

Any actual assessment would require the relevant product, actor, date and authorisation conditions, together with evidence of any SFC request and any applicable additional requirements. The reserved power to impose requirements is not evidence that it has been exercised.

The proposed readings were assessed against all delivered extracts, but the central grammatical and substantive analysis remains unfinished because the operative material was not delivered. No source-supported rival reading can presently be preferred or rejected.
